name: Acids, Bases and the Purity Tag

pages.text: An acid gives up a proton, a base takes one; $(thing)pH = −log₁₀[H⁺]$(). On the $(item)Titration Bench$() a standard runs into the sample until the indicator turns: at the endpoint the pH jumps six units in a drop. Set the titrant so the pH sits between 4 and 10 and the reagent comes out $(thing)assayed$().

Assayed reagents carry the $(thing)purity tag$(). The chemical catalysts - Zeolite, Iron, Vanadium and the Platinum-Rhodium Gauze - are poisoned by impurities: each run on an acid, base or sulfur dioxide feed that has $(l)not$() been assayed costs them five runs of life. Pipes and ME networks keep the tag; a containment cell does not. An assayed fluid says so in its name ("Ammonia (Assayed)") and shows a bright hatched border round its icon, in a tank and in an ME terminal alike.
